correctness.rationale: The claim is finite and its exact full domain is 1023 nonempty Petersen vertex subsets at every integer threshold 1..10. The standalone code compares two independent induced-component enumerations, reduces the complete mod-two filtered boundary matrix, reconstructs per-stage boundary ranks and 279 inclusion ranks independently, and checks the uniqueness of every strict coface in the sixty elementary collapses. Standard persistence reduction plus exact exhaustive enumeration proves all asserted intervals; every collapse preserves the target K_2. Mod-two experiments are not extrapolated to infinite families or integral barcodes.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a canonical symmetric ten-vertex girth-five cubic graph. The result classifies its entire natural bounded-induced-component filtration rather than an arbitrary selected count; it distinguishes a unique degree-three class persisting across three thresholds from 195 short bars, and supplies a stronger independently replayable integral simplicial-collapse certificate at the r=2→3 stability step. This provides a motivated exact benchmark for higher-independence persistence beyond the graph classes where structural theory currently applies; the numerical computation is exhaustive, not a routine renaming of an already tabulated barcode.
